niche.diet: Host blood, mucus, and gill tissue

links: Relies on moonlight for navigation and host location
Moon 1.2 Luna mass gives bright nights

skill.effect: Bathed in moonlight, the creature strikes with heightened ferocity, momentarily paralyzing its host.

chains.weakness: Inactive at new moon; cannot hunt without moonlight.
observe: Rests in crevices at new moon

plausibility.summary: Tie activity to lunar-spring high tides and nocturnal cleaning-predator avoidance: peak attachment when the tidal causeway floods (F13) and hosts (e.g. Cuarteta) pack the shallows; moonlight aids navigation on bright nights but electroreception/chemoreception still allow reduced feeding at new moon in turbid water (F20). Weaken skill weakness to ‘−damage / sluggish at new moon,’ not total shutdown.
fixes: Tie activity to lunar-spring high tides and nocturnal cleaning-predator avoidance: peak attachment when the tidal causeway floods (F13) and hosts (e.g. Cuarteta) pack the shallows; moonlight aids navigation on bright nights but electroreception/chemoreception still allow reduced feeding at new moon in turbid water (F20). Weaken skill weakness to ‘−damage / sluggish at new moon,’ not total shutdown.

analogues.organism: Horseshoe crabs (Limulus): spawn on spring high tides tied to lunar phase; not ‘inactive without moonlight.’ Some zooplankton diel/lunar vertical migration uses moonlight as one cue among several.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

skill.effect: Reveal host hidden by turbidity or camouflage; detect weak hosts.

chains.weakness: Sensory overload near strong electric sources or storms.

plausibility.summary: F20 selects against vision in turbid shallows; weak bioelectric fields from gill-breathing hosts are detectable at centimetre range in conductive seawater. At 3.5 cm and 2.8 g, added sensory neurons are affordable under F5 (high pO₂). Storm/noise overload near lightning (F8) or strong ambient fields is a fair weakness.
fixes: F20 selects against vision in turbid shallows; weak bioelectric fields from gill-breathing hosts are detectable at centimetre range in conductive seawater. At 3.5 cm and 2.8 g, added sensory neurons are affordable under F5 (high pO₂). Storm/noise overload near lightning (F8) or strong ambient fields is a fair weakness.

analogues.organism: Elasmobranch ampullae of Lorenzini (sharks, rays) detecting prey biofields; weak electric sense also in some bony fish and amphibian larvae—not homologous to arachnids but same physics.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: High atmospheric pressure increases gas solubility

skill.effect: The creature launches a swift strike to firmly attach itself to its host, briefly propelling them forward.

chains.weakness: Suffocates rapidly if removed from water.

plausibility.summary: Re-root in F5/D10 (high pO₂) + small body size; note supplementary branchial or ventral plate exchange if hosts damage dorsal skin—keeps ‘suffocates in air’ honest.
fixes: Re-root in F5/D10 (high pO₂) + small body size; note supplementary branchial or ventral plate exchange if hosts damage dorsal skin—keeps ‘suffocates in air’ honest.

analogues.organism: Monogenean flatworms and small ectoparasitic crustaceans (e.g. Argulus) rely heavily on tegument/cuticle gas exchange; amphibian skin respiration shows the size limit.

skill.effect: The creature clamps tightly onto its host, holding on firmly and resisting any attempts to dislodge it.

chains.weakness: Vulnerable to shellfish claws and cleaning behaviors.

plausibility.summary: Call sensors ‘prosomal palps’ or pit-organs (homoplasy with Lorenini), not antennae; optionally clarify lineage as chelicerate radiation from seed stock, not Earth arachnid copy. Check host size: 3.5 cm is plausible on medium shallow hosts but should be rare on the smallest Cuarteta juveniles (Kuris-style equilibrium size).

secrets: Larvae filter-feed on drifting carcass particles.
Nocturnal variant emits faint bioluminescence under full moon.
Albinos have reduced electroreception and are blind in turbid water.
Clusters of larvae form drift-nets that trap small prey.
Fossilized in volcanic tuff shows ancient arachnid ancestor.
moments: Under the full moon, the shallow causeway floods, and the water surface shimmers with a thousand tiny Aguijuela as they swarm over a stranded jellyfish.

journal.en: It feels the pulse and strikes.
